negative_controls.description: The designed assertion (process-table count == M) is run against the eager per-session spawn. It must fail there so a stuck-green counter cannot pass.
A disable written at project scope while enablement is resolved at user scope. The config file looks disabled; the process table must still list the server.

report.answer: Yes on this Linux sandbox. N=3 sessions x M=4 servers: eager policy produced 12 processes (N*M=12); shared policy produced 4 (equal to M). Disabling charlie at inert scope project left 1 live process(es) despite config saying disabled. The same disable at effective scope user produced process-table count -1. Live Cursor/Claude MCP config was not mutated.

historical_claim.note: Catalog memory of the estate incident. This unit re-proves the scaling law on a sandbox N,M rather than replaying 23x65 on a shared box.

observations.name: inert-scope disable process-table count

report.question: After opening N sessions against M MCP-style servers, does the OS process table show designed scaling (one shared process per enabled server) rather than N*M eager multiplication, and does a disable at the effective config scope produce a zero process-table count for that server while a disable at an inert scope does not?
report.title: Eager per-session MCP process multiplication
